title: Minimum Time for K Connected Components
summary: Given an integer n and an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array of edges where each edge can be removed at a specific time, and an integer k, find the minimum time t such that removing all edges with a time less than or equal to t results in at least k connected components.
statement: Given an integer n and an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array of edges where each edge can be removed at a specific time, and an integer k, find the minimum time t such that removing all edges with a time less than or equal to t results in at least k connected components. Return the minimum time t. A connected component is a subgraph where every pair of vertices is connected by paths, and no vertex shares an edge with a vertex outside the subgraph.
constraints: Up to 100,000 nodes and undirected timed edges.
At time t, every edge with removal time at most t is absent.
Return the earliest time with at least k connected components.
hints: After time t, exactly edges with larger removal times remain.
Process edges from latest to earliest while unioning components.
When adding an edge would reduce components below k, its time is the earliest required removal threshold.
Reverse processing represents every interval between removal events and union-find maintains the surviving graph.
editorial: Reverse processing represents every interval between removal events and union-find maintains the surviving graph.

tests.explanation: Removing the only edge at time three creates two components.
Both edges are gone at time four, creating three components.
